title: Romualdez: No link to flood control kickbacks
summary: The camp of suspended Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez maintained there was no evidence linking him to P7.4 billion worth of kickbacks from flood control projects based on information gathered by the…

blocks.text: In this undated photo shows former House Speaker Martin Romualdez
The Philippine STAR / Boy Santos, file photo

MANILA, Philippines — The camp of suspended Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez maintained there was no evidence linking him to P7.4 billion worth of kickbacks from flood control projects based on information gathered by the Office of the Ombudsman to prepare the probable case of plunder against him.

The prosecution panel from the ombudsman’s office presented as witness Assistant Special Prosecutor II Joshua Ang Tan during the continuation of the hearing on the petition for bail in the plunder case against Romualdez before the Sandiganbayan Third Division yesterday.

Tan was a member of the special panel of prosecutors that filed the plunder charge against Romualdez, fugitive former congressman Zaldy Co, Felicito Guevarra, who recently surrendered to authorities, and Joselyn Serenio, who remains at large.

During cross-examination, Romualdez lawyer Rashel Ann Pomoy asked Tan if in the course of their fact-finding investigation they found any document or interview from witnesses that showed Romualdez “gave Co,” former House appropriations committee chairman, instructions on the national budget, to which he replied, “None.”

Tan gave the same answer when Pomoy pressed him if there was any substandard or “ghost” or non-existent flood control project and any contract named under Romualdez, as well as statements from Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) personnel or contractors that declared Romualdez received kickbacks or commissions.
He confirmed that the ombudsman’s basis for implicating Romualdez was the statement of former DPWH undersecretary Roberto Bernardo that narrated “dealings” between Romualdez and Co.

The defense panel also argued that the two properties allegedly linked to Romualdez were named under two companies – Golden Pheasant Holdings Corp. and Brightnews Corp. – that are both tied to lawyer Jose Raulito Paras as stockholder.

However, Tan maintained that Paras was used by Romualdez, reportedly his fraternity brother, as a front or conduit for the said companies to be able to acquire the subject properties in Makati City, since Paras’ income tax returns hinted his earnings could not match the value of the properties.

During redirect examination by the ombudsman’s Deputy Special Prosecutor Omar Sagadal on why Romualdez was considered the “central figure” in the flood control scandal, Tan said, “You will never be at the front of the scheme yourself, otherwise it will be pointless.”

When asked by Sandiganbayan Associate Justice Ronald Moreno, who presided over the hearing, about the status of any case against Paras, Tan confirmed the ombudsman panel is still in the process of investigating allegations of money laundering against Romualdez and Paras.

Tan told the court that the ombudsman panel gathered “all available interviews and all open-source videos,” which included Co’s video uploaded on social media accusing Romualdez of anomalies, during its fact-finding investigation and called them “leads.”

The leads were later supported by “verified independent evidence,” Tan added, such as the statements from Co’s 18 former security aides who allegedly delivered cash-filled suitcases to the house at 42 McKinley Road, also named under Romualdez, that were used as the basis for the P7.4-billion plunder case.
